title: Eierkaas (Egg Cheese)
description: Prepared with butter or margarine, eggs, and milk.
steps: Beat the eggs with some salt, pour the milk in (for 1 small egg ¾ dl, for 1 large egg 1 dl) and pour the mixture into cups greased with butter or margarine.
Place these in a pan with water that is kept just below boiling, but must not boil, as the egg cheese would then become crumbly.
Let them stand in it until the egg has set, turn them out and cut them into cubes for garnish and filling of soup.

For pressure cooker users: Beat 3 eggs with ½ l liquid, salt and spices. Fill buttered molds with this. Place them on the rack in the pressure cooker and keep the egg custard under pressure for 5 minutes. Then remove the pan from the heat and let it stand for 5 minutes before opening it. In this short time, a beautifully smooth egg custard will have been made.

title: Eiwitglazuur (Egg White Glaze)
description: Prepared with egg white, powdered sugar, and maraschino or kirsch or vanilla extract.

ingredients.name: a few drops of maraschino, kirsch or vanilla extract
ingredients.sourceText: a few drops of maraschino, kirsch or vanilla extract

steps: Sift the powdered sugar, add small amounts of egg white until a glossy mass is obtained that is so stiff that it does not run off the spoon or spatula with which you stir but stands firm.
Add the flavoring and if desired the food coloring.

Use egg white glaze for fruit cakes. Brush the shell of puff pastry, pie dough or sand-tart dough first with egg white glaze, let it dry and then add the moist filling. This prevents the baked good from becoming moist and soft.
Use this egg white glaze to make decorations on water glaze or cooking glaze. Egg white glaze hardens quickly and thus holds its shape better.

title: Engelse kerstgebakjes (English Christmas Pastries - Mince-pies)
description: A pastry dish made with butter or margarine, currants, and raisins.
steps: Sift the flour into a bowl, add the butter or margarine and cut it into the flour until it is as fine as breadcrumbs.
Add water quickly and lightly while stirring until the dough hangs together as a firm ball.
Roll it out on a floured board into a thin sheet and let the dough, which has become slack from handling, rest under a damp cloth for half an hour.
Remove the suet from its membrane, wash it, as well as the currants, raisins and peeled and cut into quarters sour apples.
Chop this all together with the citron peel until it becomes a fine mixture.
Stir in the sugar, ginger powder, lemon zest, lemon juice and crushed cloves.
Butter approximately 30 small tartlet molds, line them with a piece of dough and fill them with a little of the mixture.
Lay a layer of dough on top, press the edges firmly together and place the molds on a baking sheet in a moderately warm oven.
Let the pastries become light brown and done (approximately 20 minutes), turn them out and keep them in a tin for several days before serving.
Serve them sprinkled with powdered sugar and decorate the platter with a sprig of holly.

title: Feuilletée or Frans bladerdeeg (Puff Pastry)
description: A pastry dish made with butter or margarine or suet, flour, and salt.

ingredients.name: butter or hard margarine or calf suet
ingredients.sourceText: 100 g butter or hard margarine or calf suet

steps: Sift the flour into a bowl, add salt, place butter, margarine or fat in it and cut these with 2 knives into fairly coarse pieces.
Add, stirring as gently as possible, drippings of cold water until everything sticks together, but especially do not use too much water, as otherwise the dough would stick when rolling out.
Roll out the ball, turning it over each time, on a flour-dusted board or table with a flour-sprinkled rolling pin to a thin layer.
Carefully brush off excess flour that clings to it and fold the dough lengthwise into thirds. (Larger quantities can be folded into thirds lengthwise and widthwise.)
Let the dough, which has become soft from handling, rest in a cool place until it is stiff again (approximately 15 minutes) and repeat rolling out three times and folding three times.
Then fold it into quarters and let it rest as long as possible.
Roll it out to the desired thickness and give it the desired shape.

description: Prepared with eggs or egg, butter or margarine, and powdered sugar or white sugar.

ingredients.name: powdered sugar or crushed white sugar
ingredients.sourceText: powdered sugar or crushed white sugar

ingredients.name: applesauce, rhubarb compote, jam, or whipped cream (for second method)
ingredients.sourceText: applesauce, rhubarb compote, jam, or whipped cream (for second method)

steps: FIRST METHOD: Beat the eggs with salt, add the flour (with 1 egg also 1 dl milk) and stir out the lumps with a wooden spoon or whisk. Add the milk gradually. Melt some butter or margarine in the frying pan or heat some salad oil, pour a little batter onto it but let it run as thin as possible. Fry the crepe on one side until light brown and cooked through on fairly high heat, roll it up with 2 forks. Lay the crepes crosswise on a plate, sprinkle powdered sugar or crushed white sugar over each layer.

SECOND METHOD: Prepare the batter as described above and fry the crepes in the same way. Do not roll them up, but lay them on a round plate with an inverted small plate on top, with the fried side facing down. Spread some applesauce, rhubarb compote, jam, or whipped cream over each crepe. Lay the last crepe with the fried side up, sprinkle some powdered sugar over it and cut the crepe cake thus obtained into wedges.
THIRD METHOD: Prepare the batter as described above, but use more flour. Fry the crepes on both sides until light brown and serve them with crushed sugar.

title: Frambozenazijn (Raspberry Vinegar)
description: Prepared with vinegar, raspberries, and sugar.
steps: Take 1 kg raspberries, clean them, wash them carefully and let them stand for 24 hours, covered with the vinegar.
Then carefully pour the liquid, without stirring, onto 1 kg fresh raspberries, which have also been picked and washed, and let them stand again for 24 hours.
Repeat this procedure to get a very fragrant extract if desired once more.
Then measure the amount of juice and add 750 g sugar per liter of liquid.
Dissolve this completely in it, but make sure that the liquid does not boil.
Skim off the foam as carefully as possible and fill well-cleaned and boiled bottles with the raspberry vinegar.
Close them with boiled corks.
Serve the raspberry vinegar with water or soda water (2 spoons per glass).

title: Galantine (Galantine)
description: Prepared with veal cutlets, pork, and ox tongue.
steps: Soak the pork caul for some time in lukewarm water and wash it thoroughly clean. Wash the cutlets, pass them twice through a meat grinder and chop them finely. Cut the bacon, which has been stripped of rind and washed, into cubes, do the same with the tongue and the truffles. Beat the egg with pepper, salt and nutmeg.

Stir through the bread soaked in water or milk and squeezed out between two spoons and the remaining ingredients, until no bread pieces are visible. Form a firm, oblong ball from it, place this on the pork caul and fold it around it on all sides.

Roll the meat in a doubled cloth and tie it as tightly as possible. Bring water with plenty of salt to a boil in a large pan with a small plate in the bottom, place the galantine in it and cook it for 1 1/2 hours.
Press it afterwards (with the cloth around it) for 24 hours between 2 flat plates with a heavy weight (weights or stones) on top. Then take it out of the cloth and cut it into thin slices.

description: Prepared with sausages or sausage, lard or margarine, and flour.
steps: First manner: Rinse the sausages with lukewarm water, dry them with a clean cloth or between a piece of brown paper. Sprinkle a little flour over them and fry them in the fat or margarine over a not too hot fire to prevent the skin from bursting, brown and cooked (approximately 15 minutes). Serve the sausages with cauliflower or sauerkraut.

Shift the fish back and forth in the pan while frying
When the fish is done, let it drain well on porous paper on both sides and serve as indicated in the rules for frying fish

title: Gebakken Tong (Fried Sole)
description: Prepared with soles, salad oil or butter or margarine, and milk or breadcrumbs.

ingredients.name: 1 dl salad oil or 75 g butter or margarine
ingredients.sourceText: 1 dl salad oil or 75 g butter or margarine

ingredients.name: 1 egg white or half an egg
ingredients.sourceText: 1 egg white or half an egg

steps: First method: Clean the soles. If this has not been done by the fishmonger, do as follows: cut off the head, make an incision in the skin at the tail and strip it off all at once, remove the innards, cut off part of the tail and side fins, wash the fish well
Rub it on both sides with salt and let it lie salted on a colander for half an hour
Dry it, then coat it on both sides in flour or milk
Fry the sole in hot salad oil or browned butter on both sides until light brown and cooked through (when the fish is done, it will split along the side fins)
Let it drain on porous paper and serve with salad and mayonnaise
Second method: Clean the fish as described above. After the salt has penetrated and the fish is dried, first pass it through beaten egg or egg white mixed with water, then coat it in fine breadcrumbs
Fry it in the same way as above. When frying breaded fish, move it especially carefully by shaking the pan. Let the fish drain on porous paper and save the fat after straining it for another time

Strain them and add some lemon juice

title: Geconfijte kweeperen (Candied Quinces)
description: Prepared with quinces, water, and sugar.
steps: Wash the pears carefully, cook them for several minutes in boiling water, then peel them, cut them into quarters and remove the cores.
Bring the water and sugar to a boil, add the fruit and if desired the spices and some of the peels and pits bound in a piece of cheesecloth.
Let everything simmer gently together until the pears are cooked and have become a nice red color (1 to 2 hours).
Place them with the liquid in a bowl and let them stand until the next day.
See if the liquid has become syrupy.
If not, cook the syrup down until it coats a cold spoon dipped into it.
Cook the fruit for 5 minutes more and place the mass in a well-cleaned Cologne pot.
Check after several days to see if the syrup is the right consistency and cook it down again if necessary.
Add lemon juice if desired.
Close the pot with damp parchment paper and label it with name and date.

ingredients.name: old bread without crust, or 150 g bread and no egg
ingredients.sourceText: 75 g old bread without crust, or 150 g bread and no egg

ingredients.name: at least 100 g butter, margarine or fat
ingredients.sourceText: at least 100 g butter, margarine or fat

steps: Beat the egg with the salt, pepper and nutmeg.
Soak the bread in some water or milk, press it out well, add the spices and salt and stir this all through the egg until it is evenly mixed with it.
Add the ground meat and stir everything with two spoons until it has become an even mass and no bread pieces are visible.
Form 2 (or more) firm balls from it.
Make butter, margarine or fat hot in a braising pan or small roasting pan.
Place the ground meat in it, sprinkle it optionally with some breadcrumbs and braise it brown and done (45 minutes per 600 g, with pork ground meat in 50 minutes per 600 g).
Finish the gravy with water or milk and with the lean gravy leftovers.

title: Gehakt in Deeg (Ground Meat in Dough for 8 Persons)
description: Prepared with veal, pork, and butter or margarine.

ingredients.name: pepper, salt and nutmeg to taste
ingredients.sourceText: pepper, salt and nutmeg to taste

steps: Put the flour in a bowl, make a small well in the middle, add the yeast and stir from the middle gradually the lukewarm milk, the melted butter or margarine and the eggs, which have been beaten with salt.
Rub out the lumps from this batter and let it rise covered (1/2 hour to 3 quarters of an hour).
Roll it out on a floured sheet, lay the ground meat mixed with the seasonings on it and roll it in firmly.
Give it the shape of a loaf or place it in a bread mold brushed with butter.
Bake it on a baking sheet in a fairly warm oven light brown and done (about 3 quarters to 1 hour) and serve it hot with curry sauce or cold.

title: Gehakt met Citroensaus en Rijst (Ground Meat with Lemon Sauce and Rice)
description: A sauce made with meat, lemon, and rice.
steps: Mix the ground meat with soaked bread, spices, finely chopped onion and egg white.
Form 4 oblong balls from this mixture and roll them in flour.
Make the butter light brown in a pan, add the flour and stir until the flour is light brown.
Add the bouillon, let the sauce cook, add the grated lemon zest and braise the meat balls in it until cooked (approximately 1/2 hour).
Remove the meat, strain the sauce and finish it with lemon juice and egg yolk.
Cook the rice in the usual manner, press it in rinsed eggcups and make a ring of it on a flat meat platter.
Place the meat in the middle and pour the sauce over the meat.

title: Gehakt met Harde Eieren (Ground Meat with Hard-Boiled Eggs for 8 Persons)
description: Prepared with eggs, veal, and bread.

ingredients.name: pepper, salt and nutmeg to taste
ingredients.sourceText: pepper, salt and nutmeg to taste

steps: Beat the egg with salt, pepper and nutmeg.
Soak the bread in some water or milk, squeeze it firmly between two spoons and stir it through the egg until it is evenly mixed with it.
Add the parsley and the ground meat and stir everything with two spoons until it becomes an even mass and no bread pieces are visible.
Press the ground meat into a 1 1/2 cm thick layer on a floured dish.

Lay the hard-boiled eggs in the middle, with the ends cut off on both sides to fit them well together, in a row one after the other, after the eggs without ends have been passed through egg white loosened with water.
Fold the ground meat around them, but make sure the eggs do not protrude at the sides.

Roll the ball through the egg white loosened with water, then through breadcrumbs and fry it in the butter or margarine, which has been made light brown in the roasting pan, brown and done (45 to 50 minutes).
Remove the ground meat from the roasting pan, slice it thinly with a sharp knife when it has cooled completely and arrange these slices overlapping on the dish.
Garnish with scalloped lemon slices, fresh sprigs of parsley and, if desired, some chopped aspic in different colors.

title: Gemarineerde Haring (Marinated Herring)
description: Prepared with herrings, peppercorns, and bay leaves.
steps: Soak the herrings for 24 hours in water with some milk, refreshing the water as needed
Cut them open along the belly side, remove the entrails, but leave the head and skin attached
Wash them thoroughly inside and out
Arrange them in a well-cleaned large bottle, so that the head of one herring lies against the tail of the previous one
Arrange the bay leaves, pieces of Spanish pepper, sliced lemon slices and onion slices between the wall of the bottle and the herrings
Place the remaining spices in the middle and pour vinegar over the herrings until they are covered
Store for at most 4 weeks, as otherwise the bones will entirely dissolve

title: Gerookte Ham (Smoked Ham)
description: Prepared with ham and water.
steps: Weigh the smoked raw ham, brush it well clean, wash it with lukewarm water and soak it for 24 hours in cold water.
Place it in boiling water, just enough to cover it and cook it gently (approximately 25 to 30 minutes per 500 g).
Test if the ham is done by seeing if the rind comes off easily.
Cut it off warm from the part that will be used and keep the rest of the ham under the rind.
Serve the ham cold or warm sliced thin, for example with garden beans and brown butter.

Note: When cooking only a piece of the ham, hang the remaining part in a linen or brown paper bag in a cool place, where the ham is well protected from flies. The liquid in which ham has been cooked can be used for pea soup, it is usually fatty, more or less salty, but not aromatic.

title: Gestoofde Paling (Braised Eel)
description: Prepared with eel, butter or margarine, and lemon.
steps: METHOD 1: Clean the eel in the usual way (see cooked eel recipe 190), wash the pieces and rub them with pepper and salt. Place the butter or margarine in small lumps in the fireproof dish, sprinkle some breadcrumbs over it and lay a few thin slices of lemon on top. Baste the eel repeatedly with a little of the liquid.

METHOD 2: First cook the cleaned eel in boiling salted water (approximately 5 minutes, depending on the thickness of the eel). Then place the pieces in the fireproof dish and treat them further as braised fish (recipe 219).

Leave small pears whole, but in this case peel the stems thinly.
Wash them and set them on with enough boiling water so they are half submerged, with the lemon peel or cinnamon stick.
Let them cook gently, shaking occasionally, for 3 to 4 hours.
If the pears do not cook red, add berry juice and sugar half an hour before they are done.
If the fruits do cook red, let only some sugar cook with them for the last 1/4 hour.
Remove the flavoring agent and bind the liquid with some mixed sago.

Grind the peeled almonds finely, mix them with sugar, the beaten egg and the grated lemon zest and pass the almond mixture through the mill once more.

title: Gevulde kool (Stuffed Cabbage)
description: Prepared with cabbage, veal, and pork.
steps: Carefully remove all leaves from the cabbage, wash them and cook them for 15 to 20 minutes in plenty of boiling salted water.
Let them drain in a colander.
Meanwhile, prepare the mince in the usual way, but make sure it is not too dry, as it becomes difficult to handle.
Place a washed white cloth in a colander or deep bowl, carefully arrange a layer of the largest cabbage leaves in it and spread a layer of mince over it.
Place another layer of leaves on top, then mince again and continue in this way until everything is used.
Bind the cloth tightly with string around the cabbage and cook it for 1.5 hours in plenty of boiling salted water, but make sure a plate lies at the bottom of the pan to prevent burning.
Remove the cabbage from the cloth, place it with the smooth side up in a fireproof small dish, pour some bouillon or jus with water over it.
Season to taste with Maggi's Aroma, sprinkle breadcrumbs over the cabbage, place pieces of butter or margarine on top and let the cabbage become light brown in the oven.

title: Haas (Roasted Hare)
description: Prepared with hare, butter or margarine, and bacon.
steps: Clean the hare or (preferably) wipe it with a damp cloth.
Cut the larding bacon into very thin strips and lard the back with one row of bacon strips, the hind quarters with two rows.
Rub the hare inside and outside with some salt.
Heat the butter or margarine thoroughly (but not brown) in a hare pan or roasting pan, place the hare in it, baste it on all sides and put it in the oven.
Place the lid over the hare pan, over the roasting pan place a piece of gray paper smeared with butter or margarine and baste the meat frequently.
Add some water to the butter when it threatens to brown.
After 2 to 2½ hours, depending on the weight of the hare, test whether the hare is done by seeing if the meat from the hind quarter can be easily removed with a spoon.

Remove it from the pan, make the butter so hot that a crust forms on the bottom of the pan, let it cool on low heat and gradually add hare blood mixed with some red wine, cream or water while stirring.
Let the gravy simmer briefly while stirring.
Remove the strings and pegs from the hare before serving and serve with apple sauce or red cabbage.

Note: You can also first cut the hare into pieces, place them for 24 hours in water and vinegar with a couple of bay leaves, some cloves and some white peppercorns, then brown and roast them. The gravy can optionally be finished with some of the liquid in which the hare was soaked.

title: Halve Gedraaide (Dutch Cold Meat Salad)
description: A salad made with meat, potatoes, and onions.
steps: Mash the potatoes, mix them with the chopped meat, 3 chopped onions and 3 snipped or chopped gherkins.
Stir in enough salad oil, vinegar, pepper and salt until a cohesive, well-flavored mixture is obtained.
Lay the mixture on a plate, smooth it, but ensure it is slightly higher in the middle than at the edges.
Garnish with the remaining onions, gherkins, hard-boiled egg cut into quarters and fresh sprigs of parsley.
Note: Instead of oil and vinegar, one can also stir mayonnaise or salad sauce through the mixture.
